definitions.explanation: To a striking or notable degree. The adverbial form of the i-adjective 著しい. Used in formal and written contexts to describe changes, differences, or developments that are clearly evident.

examples.japanese: {技術|ぎじゅつ}が{著|いちじる}しく{進歩|しんぽ}した。
{成績|せいせき}が{著|いちじる}しく{低下|ていか}している。
{公正|こうせい}さを{著|いちじる}しく{欠|か}く{判断|はんだん}だと{批判|ひはん}された。
examples.english: It was criticized as a judgment that conspicuously lacked fairness.

notes:
The adverbial form of the i-adjective {著|いちじる}しい (remarkable, conspicuous). Used in formal and written contexts to indicate a striking degree of change or difference.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {著|いちじる}しく{増加|ぞうか}する (increase remarkably)
- {著|いちじる}しく{低下|ていか}する (decline significantly)
- {著|いちじる}しく{進歩|しんぽ}する (advance remarkably)
- {著|いちじる}しく{欠|か}く (conspicuously lack)
- {著|いちじる}しく{異|こと}なる (differ markedly)

REGISTER:
Primarily used in formal writing: news reports, academic papers, legal documents, and official statements. In legal contexts, {著|いちじる}しく{不当|ふとう} (grossly unfair) is a standard legal phrase.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- とても/すごく: very (casual, everyday)
- {非常|ひじょう}に: extremely (formal but more common)
- {著|いちじる}しく: conspicuously (formal, emphasizes the visible/measurable nature of change)
